name: Reachable Assertion
principle: The product contains assert() or a similar fatal check that attacker-controlled input can make fail. A failed reachable assertion can abort the process or raise an unchecked fatal error, causing denial of service beyond the attacker's own session.
detection_signals: C/C++ assert(expr) where expr reads argv, getenv(), recv(), read(), fread(), request buffer, or parsed packet fields
C/C++ abort(), __builtin_trap(), std::terminate(), or assert(0) inside an externally reachable parser/request handler branch
Java assert request.getParameter(...), assert servlet/header/body value, or assert method argument in public/API entrypoint
Java throw new AssertionError(...) or Objects.requireNonNull(...) used as the only validation for external request data
Rust panic!(), assert!(), debug_assert!(), unwrap(), or expect() on Result/Option derived from network/file/CLI/request input
Protocol/file format parser uses assert on length, count, enum, magic, index, or range fields read from untrusted input
Single request/connection handler contains fatal assertion failure that exits the shared server process
negative_signals: Input-dependent condition is checked first with if (...) return error/throw checked controlled exception before any assert
assert condition depends only on constants, compile-time invariants, or private internal state not influenced by external input
assert is present only in test code, fuzz harness, debug-only tooling, or unreachable-by-production-request code
Fatal check is inside a per-request sandbox/worker whose crash is isolated and supervised without dropping other sessions
Rust unwrap()/expect() is on a constant literal parse or value just constructed as Some/Ok in the same statement/block
false_defense_traps: Using assert for input validation because Java assertions are disabled by default unless -ea is used
Compiling C/C++ with NDEBUG to remove assert, which also removes the validation and may expose later unsafe behavior
Catching generic Exception in Java, which does not catch AssertionError because it is an Error
Relying on debug_assert! in Rust for validation, which is removed in release builds
Logging before abort()/panic() without returning a recoverable error
verification_focus: Can an attacker-controlled input path make an assertion or equivalent fatal check fail and terminate more than the attacker's own operation?

consequence_chains.trigger: Off-by-one length/count calculation reaches an asserted invariant
Unchecked return value leaves invalid state that later violates an assertion
consequence_chains.consequence: Denial of service by assertion failure

patch_principle: Do not use assertions to validate public API arguments or untrusted input; use normal if checks and controlled error returns.
Keep assertions only for internal invariants that external input cannot falsify.
Validate lengths, ranges, indexes, formats, and required fields before parsing or state changes.
Replace abort/panic/AssertionError paths in request handling with recoverable errors that affect only the current request.
Ensure production behavior is safe whether assertions are enabled or disabled.

minimal_examples.vuln: String email = request.getParameter("email_address"); assert email != null;
minimal_examples.safe: String email = request.getParameter("email_address"); if (email == null) return badRequest("email_address is required");
